activity: Independent penetration testing (application, API, external network)
why_purchased: Customer due diligence and contracts; SOC 2 auditors commonly look for it as evidence under CC4.1 and CC7.1 though SOC 2 does not mandate it; insurer applications; PCI DSS 11.4 if in scope; the Secure Construction Standard plans an external test for Unbound.
legally_required: Not required by any statute located for a US DAF administration SaaS. Required by PCI DSS 11.4.2/11.4.3 if Echelon is in PCI scope (not established); by FedRAMP if pursued; DORA Art. 26 TLPT binds only identified EU financial entities and their in-scope ICT providers.
independence_required: PCI: organizational independence of the tester, internal resource allowed, QSA or ASV not required. FedRAMP: recognized 3PAO for JAB P-ATO; agency AO designee otherwise. DORA TLPT: internal testers only with competent authority approval, external threat intelligence and external testers every three tests. Customers: independence expectation is market practice, not verified quantitatively.
qualifications_or_accreditation: PCI: 'qualified' with no mandated certification; PCI guidance lists OSCP, CEH, GPEN, GWAPT, GXPN, CREST and CHECK as non-required examples and says certifications alone are insufficient. FedRAMP: team lead must hold an industry-recognized pen test credential. UK schemes: CHECK (NCSC) and CREST (CBEST). DORA Art. 27: certified by an accreditation body or adherence to codes of conduct, professional indemnity insurance.
internal_work_can_satisfy: Partly. Internal testing is permissible under PCI only with organizational independence from management of the target, which a very small organization may be unable to demonstrate. Internal testing is first-party evidence and cannot be labeled independent. It cannot satisfy FedRAMP or customer contracts that name third-party testing.
open_source_substitutes: ZAP, Nuclei, Schemathesis, garak, PyRIT support testing but do not substitute for a human-led test of authorization and financial business logic.
scope_reduction: Small attack surface by construction (Limen boundary, single data access path, no user HTML), threat models, test accounts, architecture and data flow documentation, prior automated scan results and fixed known issues let testers spend hours on authorization, tenant isolation and money movement. See DD-COST-001.
evidence_sharing_across_products: Shared platform components can be tested once per version and referenced by later product tests if the build and configuration are identical and the report scope says so; product-specific surfaces still need testing.
continuous_performance: Post-launch: internal continuous DAST and API fuzzing, plus a vulnerability disclosure policy or bug bounty; retest after significant change (PCI language) or major releases.
typical_cost_range: Hourly labor reference only: labor categories containing 'penetration' n=445, p25 $125.86, median $157.03, p75 $196.59 per hour (GSA CALC+ federal MAS ceiling hourly rates, snapshot 2026-11-25 (SRC-GSA-CALC); ceiling rates, not commercial engagement quotes). Vendor marketing (Software Secured): $5,000 to $100,000 or more per test; human-led authenticated web plus external network $15,000 to $50,000.
substitution_risks: Replacing with internal or automated testing would misstate assurance, miss business logic and authorization flaws, and likely fail customer and insurer requirements.
likely_customer_acceptance: Independent third-party report or attestation letter: high (expected). Internal report: low for financial-sector buyers (assumption; to be measured).
total_cost_of_ownership: External fee plus internal preparation (environment, accounts, documentation), coordination during test, remediation engineering, retest fee, and report handling under NDA. Repeats at least annually and after significant change.

why_purchased: Continuous hygiene; SOC 2 CC7.1 evidence; customer questionnaires; PCI DSS 11.3.1 internal scans if in scope.
legally_required: No statute located. PCI DSS 11.3.1 if in scope.
independence_required: PCI: internal scans may be performed by qualified internal staff reasonably independent of the system scanned; QSA or ASV not required.
internal_work_can_satisfy: Yes, for non-PCI purposes and for PCI internal scans with reasonable independence.
open_source_substitutes: Trivy, Grype, OSV-Scanner, Nuclei, ZAP baseline, Checkov; OpenSSF Scorecard for repository hygiene.
scope_reduction: Immutable images, minimal base images, locked dependencies and few exposed services reduce findings volume.
evidence_sharing_across_products: High: one pipeline and SARIF normalization serve every Echelon repository.
continuous_performance: Yes: per commit, per image build and scheduled rescans for new advisories.
typical_cost_range: Hourly labor reference only: labor categories containing 'vulnerab' n=176, p25 $101.35, median $133.3, p75 $182.43 per hour (GSA CALC+ federal MAS ceiling hourly rates, snapshot 2026-11-25 (SRC-GSA-CALC); ceiling rates, not commercial engagement quotes). Commercial scanner license prices: unknown (not public in sources reviewed).
cost_source_type: government rate data; license prices unknown
substitution_risks: Open-source data feeds and rules may lag; false negatives on F# code paths are not addressed by these tools; triage burden.
likely_customer_acceptance: High for internal scanning as an operating control when evidence is current and reviewed (assumption).
total_cost_of_ownership: No license fee for open-source tools; engineering time to integrate, tune, triage and maintain; CI compute.

why_purchased: PCI DSS 11.3.2 for in-scope internet-facing systems.
legally_required: Contractually required under PCI DSS when in scope; Echelon PCI scope not established.
independence_required: Must be performed by a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor using its approved scan solution.
qualifications_or_accreditation: ASV company qualified by PCI SSC; ASV employees re-certify every 12 months.
internal_work_can_satisfy: No. Internal or open-source scans cannot replace ASV scans.
open_source_substitutes: None acceptable for 11.3.2; internal scans can pre-check before the ASV run.
scope_reduction: Keep cardholder data out of Echelon systems (for example hosted payment pages by a processor) to shrink or remove PCI scope; applicability must be decided with the acquirer or QSA.
evidence_sharing_across_products: Possible across products sharing the same in-scope external IPs.
continuous_performance: At least once every three months and after significant change, with rescans.
typical_cost_range: Unknown: no ASV price found in credible public sources.
substitution_risks: Non-compliance with PCI DSS if substituted.
total_cost_of_ownership: Vendor fee plus remediation and dispute handling each quarter.

why_purchased: Identify control gaps before an examination; often bundled by auditors or compliance platforms.
independence_required: No for the readiness work itself. Whether a CPA firm that performs readiness can later perform the examination depends on AICPA independence rules (not reviewed in this session: unknown).
internal_work_can_satisfy: Yes. Unbound's 89-control matrix and SOC2-001..032 directive are already a readiness design, though all controls are status Designed.
open_source_substitutes: This repository's controls, evidence requirements and answer units; Praxis and Tutela evidence.
scope_reduction: Narrow system description and boundaries; inherit controls from cloud providers via their SOC reports (complementary subservice organization controls).
evidence_sharing_across_products: High if Echelon runs one shared control environment for all products.
likely_customer_acceptance: Customers do not accept readiness as assurance.
total_cost_of_ownership: Mostly internal time; optional external fee.

why_purchased: Customer and partner requirement for service organization assurance on control design at a point in time.
legally_required: No statute; contractual and market driven.
independence_required: Yes. Attestation examination by an independent CPA under AICPA attestation standards (AT-C 205).
qualifications_or_accreditation: Licensed CPA firm; AICPA peer review applies to firms performing accounting and auditing work.
internal_work_can_satisfy: No. Internal evidence can only feed the examination.
scope_reduction: System boundary design, carve-out of subservice organizations, fewer in-scope systems, automated evidence.
evidence_sharing_across_products: One report can cover several products if described in one system description (auditor decision).
continuous_performance: Point in time; usually a step toward Type II.
typical_cost_range: Vendor marketing (Vanta): SOC 2 audit fee 'usually runs between $10,000 and $50,000' (not split by type). No credible independent public source found.
substitution_risks: Any internal 'SOC 2-aligned' report risks being read as attestation; must be labeled first-party.
likely_customer_acceptance: Accepted as interim; many financial buyers ask for Type II (assumption).
total_cost_of_ownership: Auditor fee, internal preparation, management assertion and representation letter, remediation.

why_purchased: Customer requirement for assurance that controls operated effectively over a period.
legally_required: No statute; contractual and market driven.
scope_reduction: As Type I; continuous automated evidence reduces sample pulls and auditor time (hypothesis).
typical_cost_range: Vendor marketing (Vanta) only, as for Type I; page states Type 2 costs more than Type 1 without figures.
likely_customer_acceptance: High; the common expectation for SaaS vendors handling financial data (assumption).
total_cost_of_ownership: Recurring auditor fee, evidence operations all year, remediation, bridge letters.

why_purchased: International and enterprise customer requirement; alternative or complement to SOC 2.
independence_required: Yes, certification body impartiality under ISO/IEC 17021-1 and 27006-1.
qualifications_or_accreditation: Accredited certification body (accreditation by a national accreditation body to ISO/IEC 17021-1 with 27006-1).
internal_work_can_satisfy: No for certification; the standard itself requires internal audits and management review that internal staff can perform.
scope_reduction: ISMS scope definition; audit time under ISO/IEC 27006-1 depends on scope and personnel (tables not read).
evidence_sharing_across_products: High with one ISMS; SOC 2 evidence largely reusable.
typical_cost_range: Vendor marketing (Secureframe): audit costs about $10,000 to $50,000; about $10,000 per year surveillance. No credible independent source found.
likely_customer_acceptance: Accepted by many international buyers; US financial buyers often prefer SOC 2 (assumption).
total_cost_of_ownership: Certification and surveillance fees, ISMS operation, internal audit.

why_purchased: Reduce auditor hours and internal disruption.

substitution_risks: Evidence integrity and completeness must be demonstrable to auditors.

internal_work_can_satisfy: Yes; this repository's answer units are designed for it.
open_source_substitutes: This knowledge base; CSA CAIQ as a shareable standard response.

why_purchased: Sponsors' financial statement auditors rely on it when Unbound records ledgers, fund balances, NAV and unitization, fees and grant payments that flow into sponsors' financial statements (ANS-AUD-002, ANS-FCT-004, ANS-RCN-005). Added 2026-11-25 fix pass (OBJ-SOC2AUD-002).
legally_required: No statute requires Echelon to obtain one. User auditors may otherwise need to test Unbound directly or perform substantive procedures; contracts with sponsors may require it.
independence_required: Yes: independent CPA firm under AICPA attestation standards (SSAE 18, AT-C 320). The same firm should not also perform readiness or design work that would impair independence (AICPA independence rules not reviewed at primary source).
qualifications_or_accreditation: Licensed CPA firm with current AICPA peer review.
internal_work_can_satisfy: No. Internal control testing is first-party and cannot substitute.
scope_reduction: Report as of the production go-live date covering ledger posting, NAV and unitization, fee computation, grant authorization, payment file preparation, reconciliation, change and logical access (ANS-AUD-001 roadmap).
evidence_sharing_across_products: Shares control environment, change and access testing with SOC 2, but has separate control objectives, system description and report; restricted use limits sharing to user entities and their auditors.
continuous_performance: One-time point-in-time report, followed by Type 2.
typical_cost_range: Unknown. No credible public cost source located; a separate examination from SOC 2, so additive to SOC 2 fees.
cost_sources: none (SRC-AICPA-SOC1-GUIDE and SRC-AICPA-SSAE-18 describe the engagement, not its cost)
substitution_risks: A SOC 2 report does not address control objectives relevant to user entities' financial reporting; presenting it as a SOC 1 substitute misleads user auditors.
likely_customer_acceptance: Expected by sponsors' auditors when Unbound is a financial reporting system (assumption, not measured).
total_cost_of_ownership: Auditor fee, system description and control objectives drafting, management assertion, internal preparation; restricted-use distribution handling.

why_purchased: Sponsors' financial statement auditors rely on it when Unbound records ledgers, fund balances, NAV and unitization, fees and grant payments that flow into sponsors' financial statements (ANS-AUD-002, ANS-FCT-004, ANS-RCN-005). Added 2026-11-25 fix pass (OBJ-SOC2AUD-002).
legally_required: No statute requires Echelon to obtain one. User auditors may otherwise need to test Unbound directly or perform substantive procedures; contracts with sponsors may require it.

evidence_sharing_across_products: Shares control environment, change and access testing with SOC 2, but has separate control objectives, system description and report; restricted use limits sharing to user entities and their auditors.
continuous_performance: Annual recurring period aligned to sponsors' fiscal years; bridge letters for gaps.
typical_cost_range: Unknown. No credible public cost source located; a separate examination from SOC 2, so additive to SOC 2 fees.
cost_sources: none (SRC-AICPA-SOC1-GUIDE and SRC-AICPA-SSAE-18 describe the engagement, not its cost)
substitution_risks: A SOC 2 report does not address control objectives relevant to user entities' financial reporting; presenting it as a SOC 1 substitute misleads user auditors.
likely_customer_acceptance: Expected by sponsors' auditors when Unbound is a financial reporting system (assumption, not measured).
total_cost_of_ownership: Recurring auditor fee, evidence operations all year, complementary user entity control documentation per sponsor, bridge letters, remediation. Likely the largest recurring assurance cost for a fund administration platform (judgment, not sourced).
